The test image shows a corn stalk with tan/straw coloring and distinct **diamond-shaped dark brown lesions** on the stalk surface. The stalk appears dried with a pithy interior visible at the cut end. This pattern points strongly toward a stalk disease.

Top candidates:
- **Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback** — anthracnose stalk rot is known for diamond-shaped lesions on stalk
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot** — bleached stalk, white mycelium
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot** — shredded gray pith

The diamond-shaped lesions are most characteristic of Anthracnose. Let me verify with one reference.

The reference for Anthracnose shows the leaf form (elongated dark necrotic lesions on green leaf). The test image shows the **stalk form** with distinct diamond-shaped brown lesions on a tan dried stalk — this is classic anthracnose stalk rot, caused by the same pathogen (*Colletotrichum graminicola*) and falls under the Anthracnose class.

The diamond-shaped lesions are diagnostic — no other stalk disease produces this pattern. Diplodia shows white mycelium at nodes; Charcoal rot shows shredded gray pith with sclerotia. Neither matches the test image.
